body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 49d8889aebc10185d8e1876e0c39d69f83ada314 -->
Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is an independent second review. The change sets posted G-code refusal behavior, so it is safety-floor work under AGENTS.md.

**What looks good**

- The post refuses a positive G84 and G85 dwell by name before it positions or writes the cycle. It never drops the dwell silently (Prime Directive).
- The refused hole records its cycle coordinates (`cycX/cycY/cycR`, `inCycle`). The hole's expanded cuts do not leak as plain G1 feeds. This matches the named-refusal contract of #1819 and the pattern in `assets/posts/heidenhain.cps:634`.
- The refusal tests the requested seconds before the rounding to milliseconds. A sub-millisecond dwell cannot round away silently.
- The refusal wording matches the Fanuc-family wording of #2387. The G84 text states the post's own limit; it does not claim the control lacks tapping dwell.
- Issue #2357 permits the named G84 refusal. The Siemens manual citation (behavior only) supports the G85 refusal.
- The new test file sits in `crates/post` with a Gate map line. The decision file follows the `docs/decisions/` format. No golden or snapshot files changed.

**Results, merged with main (built locally, Windows)**

- The PR branch already contains main `3e47b898b`. The trial merge gave "Already up to date". No conflicts.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: PASS, 46 steps, 0 failed, wall 1.2 min on a warm cache.
- The first gate run showed one FAIL in the "app build (--no-run)" step with a compile error. A direct `cargo test -p camcraft-app --no-run` then built clean (exit 0), and the re-run of the full quick gate passed all 46 steps. The failure was transient in this target directory; no PR file enters the app build.
- New suite `sinumerik_dwell`: 3 passed (`sinumerik_g84_dwell_is_refused_by_name`, `sinumerik_g85_dwell_is_refused_by_name`, `sinumerik_g84_and_g85_without_dwell_still_post`).
- Dwell-family suites from the gate map passed: `cycle_dwell` (9), `dwell_cycles_modal_p` (5), `g83_dwell` (7), `sinumerik_g83_dwell` (3), `ream_cycle` (5), `expanded_bore_refusal` (4), `script_sinumerik` (13).
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: PASS.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: clean.

**Requested before merge**

None.

**Notes (not blocking)**

- `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps:768`: the `g !== "G84"` clause in the P-word guard is now unreachable for a positive dwell, because the refusal at `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps:743` returns first. Keeping it as defense-in-depth is fine.
- The earlier Sinumerik refusals (`assets/posts/sinumerik.cps:737` for G73, `assets/posts/sinumerik.cps:731` for G86) return before the refused-hole tracking. A hand-built stream with an expanded chain for those holes may post the chain as plain moves. That difference predates this PR. A P7 follow-up issue may be worth it.
- No physical controller ran the output, as the body states.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
